findings.title: notification-scheduler edge function lacks authentication
findings.description: The Deno.serve entry point accepts any HTTP request without verifying an Authorization header or service-role token. Unlike email-notifications (which checks Bearer service-role key), notification-scheduler processes all incoming requests unconditionally. The function URL is publicly accessible — any external caller could trigger mass notification dispatch (push + email sends).
findings.recommendation: Add service-role bearer token verification at the top of the Deno.serve handler, identical to email-notifications/index.ts. Return 401 for unauthorized requests.

findings.title: Error response exposes internal error details
findings.description: The catch block returns `detail: String(e)` in the HTTP response, which can expose internal stack traces, file paths, or other sensitive implementation details. This is compounded by SA-001 since the endpoint has no auth.
findings.recommendation: Remove the `detail` field from the error response. Return only `{ "error": "Internal server error" }`. The full error is already logged via console.error.

filtered_findings.title: MMKV storage not encrypted
filtered_findings.description: react-native-mmkv stores data unencrypted on device filesystem. Filtered: device-level protection is the standard for this data sensitivity class.

filtered_findings.title: email-notifications request body not schema-validated
filtered_findings.description: No explicit JSON schema validation on incoming request body fields beyond TypeScript casting. Filtered: function is service-role only (auth check at entry).

filtered_findings.title: Deno module loaded from deno.land/x without integrity hash
filtered_findings.description: djwt imported from deno.land/x/djwt@v3.0.2 without a lockfile integrity check. Filtered: version is pinned; acceptable for current risk level.
